questions.:question/problem:
Determine whether the following system of equations is consistent or inconsistent. If it is consistent, indicate whether it is consistent dependent or consistent independent.
$\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 2y - 2 &=0 \\ 4x - 8y &=8\end{aligned}\right.$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x - 2y - 2 &= 0 \\
x &= 2 + 2y
\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
x=2+2y
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
4x - 8y &= 8 \\
4(2 + 2y) - 8y &= 8 \\
8 + 8y - 8y &= 8 \\
8 &= 8
\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a true statement, we conclude that there are infinitely many solutions to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent dependent.

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x - 3y &=-9 \\ -2x - 3y &=-9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x - 3y &= -9 \\ -2x &= -9 + 3y \\ x &= \frac{9}{2} - \frac{3}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{9}{2} - \frac{3}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x - 3y &= -9 \\ -2\left(\frac{9}{2} - \frac{3}{2}y\right) - 3y &= -9 \\ -9 + 3y - 3y &= -9 \\ -9 &= -9\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a true statement, we conclude that there are infinitely many solutions to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent dependent.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x &=7 - 3y \\ 3y &=8 - 3x\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x &= 7 - 3y \\ x &= \frac{7}{3} - y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{7}{3} - y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

questions.:question/problem:
Determine whether the following system of equations is consistent or inconsistent. If it is consistent, indicate whether it is consistent dependent or consistent independent.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-6x - 4y - 9 &=0 \\ -12x - 8y &=19\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6x - 4y - 9 &= 0 \\ -6x &= 9 + 4y \\ x &= -\frac{3}{2} - \frac{2}{3}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=-\frac{3}{2} - \frac{2}{3}y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}-12x - 8y &= 19 \\ -12\left(-\frac{3}{2} - \frac{2}{3}y\right) - 8y &= 19 \\ 18 + 8y - 8y &= 19 \\ 18 &= 19\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a false statement, we conclude that there are no solutions to the system. Therefore, the system is inconsistent.

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-4x + 3y &=3 \\ 2x + 4y &=-24\end{aligned}\right.
$$

This system of equations is {{field-1}}.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
A system of equations is *consistent* if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, it is called *inconsistent*.

Consistent systems, in turn, can be of the following two types:

- When a system of equations has a *single* solution, it is called *consistent independent*.
- When a system of equations has an *infinite number* of solutions, it is called *consistent dependent*.

We can summarize these definitions using the diagram shown below.

![](images/16/1692fbea298339ff839cf2f14986d51af45d1ec72b2b7d0de179336bdef40c0e.png)

We will solve the system using substitution.

First, we can solve the first equation for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x + 3y &= 3 \\ -4x &= 3 - 3y \\ x &= -\frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{4}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}x&=-\frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{4}y\end{aligned}
$$

into the second equation to obtain an equation that we can solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x + 4y &= -24 \\ 2\left(-\frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{4}y\right) + 4y &= -24 \\ -\frac{3}{2} + \frac{3}{2}y + 4y &= -24 \\ \frac{11}{2}y &= -\frac{45}{2} \\ y &= -\frac{45}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

Because we obtained a single value of $y$, and $x$ is determined by $x=-\frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{4}y$, there is exactly one solution to the system. Therefore, the system is consistent independent.
